title: Which Study Design Answers Which Question? A Decision Map

hook.en: Many research problems start with the wrong tool. A survey cannot prove a treatment works, and a trial cannot tell you how patients feel. Match the question to the design first, and half the battle is won.
hook.ur: Bohat se research masail ghalat aale se shuru hote hain. Survey sabit nahi kar sakta ke ilaaj kaam karta hai, aur trial nahi bata sakta ke mareez kaisa mehsoos karte hain. Pehle sawal ko design se milayein, aadhi jang jeet li.

goal.en: By the end, you'll choose a sensible design for a therapy, diagnosis, prognosis, risk, frequency or experience question, and say why a wrong design cannot answer a question however large it is.
goal.ur: End tak aap therapy, diagnosis, prognosis, risk, frequency ya tajurbe ke sawal ke liye munasib design chunenge, aur batayenge ke ghalat design kisi sawal ka jawab nahi de sakta chahe kitna bhi bara ho.

summaryEn: The question decides the design: effect needs comparison, frequency needs a survey, course needs a cohort, accuracy needs a diagnostic study, experience needs qualitative research.
A large study with the wrong design gives a precise but wrong answer.
Choose the design the question needs, within ethics and what you can realistically do.

next.title: Randomised Trials for Therapists — Randomisation, Blinding and Real-World Fit

title: Randomised Trials for Therapists — Randomisation, Blinding and Real-World Fit

hook.en: A randomised trial is the best tool we have for asking "does it work?", but in physiotherapy you cannot blind the therapist or the patient to an exercise class. Learn what randomisation really protects, what blinding problems mean and why a trial can be perfect and still not fit your clinic.
hook.ur: Randomised trial "kya kaam karta hai?" poochhne ka hamare paas behtareen aala hai, lekin physiotherapy mein aap exercise class mein therapist ya mareez ko blind nahi kar sakte. Seekhein ke randomisation asal mein kis cheez se bachati hai, blinding ke masail ka kya matlab hai aur trial mukammal ho kar bhi aap ke clinic ke liye kyun munasib nahi ho sakta.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain what random allocation and concealment protect against, say which people can be blinded in a physiotherapy trial, define intention-to-treat, and tell a pragmatic from an explanatory trial.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke random allocation aur concealment kis se bachate hain, batayenge physiotherapy trial mein kin logon ko blind kiya ja sakta hai, intention-to-treat ki tareef karenge, aur pragmatic ko explanatory trial se alag karenge.

summaryEn: Randomisation balances groups, concealment protects the allocation, and blinding the assessor matters most in physiotherapy trials.
Intention-to-treat analysis keeps people in their randomised group and shows what happens in practice.
Pragmatic trials fit everyday clinics better than explanatory trials; check harms and generalisability.

next.title: Cohort, Case-Control and Cross-Sectional Studies

title: Cohort, Case-Control and Cross-Sectional Studies

hook.en: You cannot randomly assign people to smoke, to lift heavy loads or to get injured. For many questions in physiotherapy, observational studies are all we have. Learn to tell the three main types apart, and to ask the one question that matters: what else could explain this?
hook.ur: Aap logon ko random tareeqe se cigarette peene, bhaari wazan uthane ya zakhmi hone ke liye tay nahi kar sakte. Physiotherapy ke bohat se sawalon ke liye observational studies hi hamare paas hain. Teen bari qismon ko alag karna seekhein, aur woh ek sawal poochhna jo ahem hai: aur kya is ki wajah ho sakta hai?

goal.en: By the end, you'll tell cohort, case-control and cross-sectional studies apart, know which questions each can answer, understand confounding and reverse causation, and read an observational result with the right caution.
goal.ur: End tak aap cohort, case-control aur cross-sectional studies ko alag karenge, jaanenge har kis sawal ka jawab de sakta hai, confounding aur reverse causation samjhenge, aur observational nateeje ko sahi ehtiyat se parhenge.

summaryEn: Cohort studies follow people forward, case-control studies look back from cases, and cross-sectional studies take a snapshot.
Observational studies show association; confounding and reverse causation can mislead.
Use words that match the design, and check what was adjusted for.

next.title: Case Reports and Case Series — Writing One Properly with CARE

title: Case Reports and Case Series — Writing One Properly with CARE

hook.en: Your first publication does not need a grant, a team or a hundred patients. It can be one patient you treated, written up carefully. A good case report teaches others, spots new problems and starts your research journey. A bad one is a diary entry. The CARE checklist is the difference.
hook.ur: Aap ki pehli publication ko grant, team ya sau mareez nahi chahiye. Yeh ek mareez ho sakta hai jis ka aap ne ilaaj kiya, ehtiyat se likha hua. Achhi case report doosron ko sikhati hai, naye masail pakadti hai aur aap ke research safar ko shuru karti hai. Buri report diary ki entry hai. CARE checklist farq hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what a case report and a case series can and cannot show, follow the CARE checklist to structure one, protect patient privacy and consent, and decide when a case is worth writing.
goal.ur: End tak aap jaanenge ke case report aur case series kya dikha sakti hain aur kya nahi, CARE checklist se ek ka dhancha banayenge, mareez ki nijiyat aur razamandi mehfooz rakhenge, aur tay karenge ke case likhne ke qabil hai ya nahi.

summaryEn: A case report describes one patient in detail; it cannot prove a treatment works but can show unusual presentations, new harms and teaching points.
Use CARE: a timeline, honest findings, the patient's view and a limited discussion.
Always get written consent, remove identifying details, and avoid advertising.

next.title: Single-Case Designs and N-of-1 Trials in Your Own Clinic

title: Single-Case Designs and N-of-1 Trials in Your Own Clinic

hook.en: Large trials tell you what works on average. But your patient is one person. An N-of-1 trial lets you test, on that one person, whether a treatment really helps them, using nothing more than a notebook and a plan.
hook.ur: Bade trials batate hain ke average mein kya kaam karta hai. Lekin aap ka mareez ek insaan hai. N-of-1 trial aap ko is ek insaan par aazmane deta hai ke ilaaj sach mein unhein faida deta hai ya nahi, sirf ek copy aur ek plan ke saath.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain what a single-case or N-of-1 design is, plan a simple A-B-A-B test for one patient, know which conditions suit it and which do not, and read the results honestly.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke single-case ya N-of-1 design kya hai, ek mareez ke liye saada A-B-A-B test plan karenge, jaanenge kin halaton mein munasib hai aur kin mein nahi, aur nateeje imaandari se parhenge.

summaryEn: A single-case or N-of-1 design uses one person as their own control across baseline and treatment phases.
It suits stable, chronic, symptom-based problems with quick on and off effects, not acute or lingering ones.
Results guide that patient's care, never withhold needed treatment, and set stopping rules.

next.title: Qualitative Research — Interviews, Focus Groups and Thematic Analysis

title: Qualitative Research — Interviews, Focus Groups and Thematic Analysis

hook.en: A trial can tell you how much pain fell. It cannot tell you why a mother stopped doing her child's exercises, or what it feels like to learn to walk again. Those answers live in words, and qualitative research knows how to listen to them.
hook.ur: Trial bata sakta hai dard kitna kam hua. Yeh nahi bata sakta ke maan ne bache ki exercises kyun chhor di, ya dobara chalna seekhna kaisa lagta hai. Yeh jawab alfaaz mein hain, aur qualitative research unhein sunna jaanti hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what qualitative research can answer, choose between interviews and focus groups, follow the steps of thematic analysis, and judge rigour using trustworthiness criteria instead of p-values.
goal.ur: End tak aap jaanenge ke qualitative research kya jawab de sakti hai, interviews aur focus groups mein se chunenge, thematic analysis ke qadam follow karenge, aur p-values ke bajaye bharosemandi ke criteria se rigour parkhenge.

summaryEn: Qualitative research explores experiences and reasons using interviews, focus groups and thematic analysis.
Choose private interviews for sensitive topics and groups for shared views.
Judge rigour by trustworthiness, not p-values, and protect participants.

next.title: Mixed-Methods Research — Numbers and Stories Together

title: Mixed-Methods Research — Numbers and Stories Together

hook.en: A trial says the programme worked a little. Interviews say patients hated the trips to clinic. Which is true? Both. Mixed-methods research puts numbers and stories in the same study so that each can explain the other.
hook.ur: Trial kehta hai programme ne thora kaam kiya. Interviews kehte hain mareez clinic ke chakkar se nafrat karte thay. Kaun sa sach hai? Dono. Mixed-methods research numbers aur kahaniyan ek hi study mein rakhti hai taake har ek doosre ki wazahat kare.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain why and when to mix methods, name the three core designs (convergent, explanatory sequential, exploratory sequential), and plan simple integration of the two kinds of data.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke tareeqe kyun aur kab milayein, teen bunyadi designs (convergent, explanatory sequential, exploratory sequential) ke naam batayenge, aur dono qism ke data ke saade integration ka plan banayenge.

summaryEn: Mixed-methods research combines numbers and stories to answer questions neither can answer alone.
Three core designs: convergent, explanatory sequential and exploratory sequential.
The key is integration, shown through a clear reason and a joint display.

next.title: Goniometry Foundations — Axis, Arms, Scale and the Six Steps

title: Goniometry Foundations — Axis, Arms, Scale and the Six Steps

hook.en: A goniometer is only as accurate as the person holding it. Learn the six steps, why the arms matter more than the axis and how to read a scale without fooling yourself.
hook.ur: Goniometer utna hi sahi hota hai jitna usay pakarne wala. Chhe steps, arms axis se zyada kyun ahem hain aur scale ko bina khud ko dhoka diye parhna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll set up any goniometric measurement in six steps, align the arms on bony landmarks, read the correct scale and record the result like a professional.
goal.ur: End tak aap kisi bhi goniometric measurement ko chhe steps mein setup karenge, arms ko bony landmarks par align karenge, sahi scale parhenge aur result professional tareeqay se likhenge.

summaryEn: Six steps for every measurement: position, stabilise, landmarks, align, move and measure, record.
Arms aligned on bony landmarks matter more than the axis; read the right scale straight on and record the change, not the dial number.
Stabilise to prevent substitution, accept about 5° error, and record the full arc, the position and any pain.

next.title: Surveys and Questionnaires — Design, Sampling and Response Bias

title: Surveys and Questionnaires — Design, Sampling and Response Bias

hook.en: Anyone can make a survey in ten minutes. Making one that gives a true answer takes more care. A leading question, a convenience sample or a 15 percent response rate can quietly make a survey say whatever you hoped it would.
hook.ur: Koi bhi das minute mein survey bana sakta hai. Aisa banana jo sachcha jawab de, zyada ehtiyat maangta hai. Rehnumai karne wala sawal, aasaani se mila sample ya 15 fisad response rate chupke se survey ko woh kehne par majboor kar sakte hain jo aap chahte thay.

goal.en: By the end, you'll write clear, neutral questions, choose a sensible sampling approach, spot response and non-response bias, and test a questionnaire before sending it.
goal.ur: End tak aap saaf, ghair jaanibdaar sawal likhenge, munasib sampling ka tareeqa chunenge, response aur non-response bias pehchanenge, aur bhejne se pehle questionnaire ko test karenge.

summaryEn: A survey is only as good as its sample, its questions and its response rate.
Write neutral, single-topic questions, pilot them and report the response rate honestly.
Size does not fix bias; protect privacy and offer a language the respondents use.

next.title: Delphi and Consensus Methods — When Experts Must Agree

title: Delphi and Consensus Methods — When Experts Must Agree

hook.en: For many questions in physiotherapy there is no trial, and experts disagree. A Delphi study asks a panel to rate and re-rate statements until they converge, which turns scattered opinion into structured agreement. It is not proof, but it is far better than the loudest voice winning.
hook.ur: Physiotherapy ke bohat se sawalon ke liye trial nahi, aur experts mutafiq nahi. Delphi study panel se bayanat ko rate aur dobara rate karwati hai jab tak woh qareeb na aa jayein, jo bikhri hui raye ko munazzam ittefaq mein badalti hai. Yeh saboot nahi, lekin sab se unchi awaaz ke jeetne se kahin behtar hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain how a Delphi study runs, pick a panel and a consensus rule, avoid common traps, and say what consensus does and does not show.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke Delphi study kaise chalti hai, panel aur consensus ka qaida chunenge, aam jaalon se bachenge, aur batayenge ke consensus kya dikhata hai aur kya nahi.

summaryEn: A Delphi study reaches structured agreement through anonymous rounds with feedback.
Fix the consensus rule beforehand, pick a diverse panel and report disagreement.
Consensus is a guide when evidence is lacking; it is not proof.

next.title: Diagnostic Accuracy Studies — Sensitivity, Likelihood Ratios and Spectrum Bias

title: Diagnostic Accuracy Studies — Sensitivity, Likelihood Ratios and Spectrum Bias

hook.en: Every special test you do was once the subject of a study. But the numbers in the paper were produced in a particular group of patients, against a particular reference test. Learn to read a diagnostic study so that you know whether a test's reported accuracy will hold in your clinic.
hook.ur: Har special test jo aap karte hain kabhi kisi study ka mauzu tha. Lekin paper ke numbers ek khaas group ke mareezon mein, ek khaas reference test ke muqabale mein bane thay. Diagnostic study parhna seekhein taake pata chale ke test ki bayan shuda durusti aap ke clinic mein bhi rahegi ya nahi.

goal.en: By the end, you'll read a 2x2 table, explain sensitivity, specificity and likelihood ratios, use the STARD and QUADAS-2 ideas to check bias, and spot spectrum bias.
goal.ur: End tak aap 2x2 table parhenge, sensitivity, specificity aur likelihood ratios samjhayenge, bias jaanchne ke liye STARD aur QUADAS-2 ke khayalat istemal karenge, aur spectrum bias pehchanenge.

summaryEn: Diagnostic studies compare an index test with a reference standard; sensitivity helps rule out, specificity helps rule in.
Likelihood ratios show how much a result changes your suspicion, and spectrum bias can inflate accuracy.
No clinical test alone excludes a serious diagnosis; combine tests, rules and judgement.

next.title: Prognostic Studies and Prediction Models — Who Will Recover?

title: Prognostic Studies and Prediction Models — Who Will Recover?

hook.en: Patients ask the question we all dread: "Will I get better, and how long will it take?" Prognosis is the honest answer to that. Learn to read a prognostic study, tell a risk factor from a prediction tool, and avoid scaring patients with labels that the evidence cannot support.
hook.ur: Mareez woh sawal poochhte hain jis se hum sab darte hain: "Kya main theek ho jaunga, aur kitna waqt lagega?" Prognosis us ka imaandar jawab hai. Prognostic study parhna seekhein, risk factor ko prediction tool se alag karein, aur mareezon ko un labels se dara-ne se bachein jin ka saboot himayat nahi karta.

goal.en: By the end, you'll tell a prognostic factor from a prediction model, explain what makes a good prognostic study (inception cohort, adequate follow-up), know why validation matters, and communicate prognosis to patients hopefully and honestly.
goal.ur: End tak aap prognostic factor ko prediction model se alag karenge, samjhayenge ke achhi prognostic study kya banata hai (inception cohort, kaafi follow-up), jaanenge validation kyun ahem hai, aur mareezon ko prognosis ummeed aur imaandari se batayenge.

summaryEn: Prognostic studies follow an inception cohort with complete follow-up; prediction models must be validated in new patients.
Risk factors, prognostic factors and prediction models are different things.
Share prognosis as a probability with hope and a plan, avoid labels, and screen red flags first.

next.title: Measurement Properties — Reliability, Validity, Responsiveness and MDC vs MCID

title: Measurement Properties — Reliability, Validity, Responsiveness and MDC vs MCID

hook.en: A goniometer reads 45 degrees today and 52 tomorrow. Did the patient improve, or is the tool noisy? Before you trust any measure, you need to know how reliable, valid and responsive it is, and how much change is real and how much is just measurement noise.
hook.ur: Goniometer aaj 45 degree aur kal 52 degree batata hai. Kya mareez behtar hua, ya aala shor wala hai? Kisi bhi naap par bharosa se pehle aap ko jaanna chahiye ke woh kitna reliable, valid aur responsive hai, aur kitni tabdeeli asal hai aur kitni sirf naap ka shor.

goal.en: By the end, you'll tell reliability from validity and responsiveness, read ICC and kappa values, explain SEM and the minimal detectable change (MDC), and separate MDC from the minimal clinically important difference (MCID).
goal.ur: End tak aap reliability ko validity aur responsiveness se alag karenge, ICC aur kappa ki values parhenge, SEM aur minimal detectable change (MDC) samjhayenge, aur MDC ko minimal clinically important difference (MCID) se alag karenge.

summaryEn: Reliability is consistency, validity is accuracy of meaning and responsiveness is detecting change.
A change must exceed the MDC to be confidently real, and exceed the MCID to matter to the patient.
Standardise your measures and never make safety decisions on a single noisy reading.

next.title: Clinical Audit, Service Evaluation and Quality Improvement (PDSA)

title: Clinical Audit, Service Evaluation and Quality Improvement (PDSA)

hook.en: You do not need a grant or a university to do research that matters. Auditing your own clinic against a standard, then improving it in small cycles, is the fastest way to raise the care your patients receive. And it is a perfect first project for any therapist.
hook.ur: Aham research karne ke liye grant ya university ki zaroorat nahi. Apne clinic ka kisi mayar ke muqabale mein audit aur phir chhote chakkron mein behtari mareezon ko milne wali care barhane ka sab se tez tareeqa hai. Aur yeh har therapist ka behtareen pehla project hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll tell audit, service evaluation, quality improvement and research apart, run a simple audit cycle, use PDSA to test a change, and report your work with SQUIRE.
goal.ur: End tak aap audit, service evaluation, quality improvement aur research mein farq karenge, saada audit chakkar chalayenge, tabdeeli aazmane ke liye PDSA istemal karenge, aur apna kaam SQUIRE se report karenge.

summaryEn: Audit checks practice against a standard; QI tests changes in small PDSA cycles; research aims at new general knowledge.
Close the loop by re-measuring after a change, and plot results on a run chart.
Protect patient data, report safety problems immediately and share what you learn.

next.title: Registries and Routine Outcome Data — Learning From Every Patient

title: Registries and Routine Outcome Data — Learning From Every Patient

hook.en: Every day a clinic generates data that could answer big questions: who recovers, how long it takes and what helps. Most of it is lost in paper files. A registry turns routine care into evidence, and routine outcome measures turn each patient into part of a bigger story.
hook.ur: Har din clinic aisa data paida karta hai jo bade sawalon ka jawab de sakta hai: kaun theek hota hai, kitna waqt lagta hai aur kya madad karta hai. Zyada tar kaghazi files mein kho jata hai. Registry routine care ko saboot mein badalti hai, aur routine outcome measures har mareez ko bari kahani ka hissa banate hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain what a patient registry is, choose a small set of routine outcomes, know the strengths and limits of registry data, and plan simple, ethical data collection in your own clinic.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke patient registry kya hai, routine outcomes ka chhota set chunenge, registry data ki khoobiyan aur hadein jaanenge, aur apne clinic mein saada, akhlaqi data collection plan karenge.

summaryEn: Registries and routine outcomes show what happens in real practice, but without comparison groups they cannot prove cause.

next.title: Implementation Science — Why Good Evidence Does Not Reach Patients

title: Implementation Science — Why Good Evidence Does Not Reach Patients

hook.en: Studies suggest it can take well over a decade for a proven treatment to become routine care, and many patients never get it. Knowing what works is only half the job. The other half is getting it done, and that is a science of its own.
hook.ur: Studies batati hain ke sabit shuda ilaaj ko routine care banne mein dehai se zyada lag sakti hai, aur bohat se mareez ko kabhi nahi milta. Yeh jaanna ke kya kaam karta hai aadha kaam hai. Doosra aadha usay karna hai, aur woh apni science hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll name common barriers to using evidence (knowledge, attitude, time, resources, system), match each with a strategy, use the CFIR domains to think about a change in your clinic, and plan a small implementation project.
goal.ur: End tak aap saboot istemal karne ki aam rukawatein (ilm, rawaiyya, waqt, wasail, nizam) batayenge, har ek ko hikmat-e-amli se milayenge, apne clinic ki tabdeeli ke baare mein sochne ke liye CFIR ke domains istemal karenge, aur chhota implementation project plan karenge.

summaryEn: Good evidence often fails to reach patients because of barriers at the individual, team, organisation and system levels.
Diagnose the barriers, match strategies to them and pilot small before spreading.
Do not blame people for system problems, and check that changes do not add risk.

next.title: Effect Sizes, Confidence Intervals and P-Values — What They Do and Do Not Mean

title: Effect Sizes, Confidence Intervals and P-Values — What They Do and Do Not Mean

hook.en: "p < 0.05" does not mean the treatment is important, and "p > 0.05" does not mean it does not work. Many clinicians misread the most quoted number in science. Learn what the p-value really says, and why the effect size and its confidence interval tell you far more.
hook.ur: "p < 0.05" ka matlab yeh nahi ke ilaaj ahem hai, aur "p > 0.05" ka matlab yeh nahi ke kaam nahi karta. Bohat se clinicians science ke sab se zyada quote kiye jane wale number ko ghalat parhte hain. Seekhein ke p-value asal mein kya kehta hai, aur effect size aur uska confidence interval aap ko kahin zyada kyun batate hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll define a p-value in one sentence, interpret an effect size and a 95 percent confidence interval, compare them with the minimal important change, and avoid the common traps such as "no significant difference means no difference".
goal.ur: End tak aap p-value ki ek jumle mein tareef karenge, effect size aur 95 fisad confidence interval ki tafseer karenge, unhein minimal important change se milayenge, aur aam jaalon se bachenge jaise "significant farq nahi matlab farq nahi".

summaryEn: Effect size says how big, the confidence interval says how precise, and the p-value says how surprising the data would be if there were no effect.
Compare the interval with the minimal important change; significance is not importance, and non-significance is not no effect.
A p-value above 0.05 never proves safety; check harm estimates and their intervals.

title: Absolute vs Relative Risk, NNT and NNH

hook.en: "Halves your risk!" sounds wonderful. But halving a risk of 2 in 100 gives 1 in 100, and that may not be worth much. Learn the two ways of describing the same result, and a number that tells you how many patients you must treat for one to benefit.
hook.ur: "Aap ka khatra aadha!" bohat achha lagta hai. Lekin 100 mein 2 ke khatre ko aadha karne se 100 mein 1 hota hai, aur shayad is ki zyada qeemat nahi. Ek hi nateeje ko bayan karne ke do tareeqe seekhein, aur woh number jo batata hai ke ek ko faida dene ke liye kitne mareezon ka ilaaj karna hoga.

goal.en: By the end, you'll calculate absolute risk reduction, relative risk reduction and the number needed to treat (NNT) from simple figures, explain the number needed to harm (NNH), and show patients risks in natural frequencies.
goal.ur: End tak aap saade figures se absolute risk reduction, relative risk reduction aur number needed to treat (NNT) nikalenge, number needed to harm (NNH) samjhayenge, aur mareezon ko khatre natural frequencies mein dikhayenge.

summaryEn: Absolute risk reduction shows the real difference; relative risk reduction can sound bigger than it is.
NNT is 1 divided by ARR, and it depends on the baseline risk.
Show patients natural frequencies and weigh NNT against NNH.

title: Goniometry of the Shoulder, Elbow and Wrist — Landmarks That Work

hook.en: Shoulder range is the hardest to measure well because the scapula, the trunk and the humerus all join in. Learn the landmarks and the tricks that make upper-limb readings repeatable.
hook.ur: Shoulder ki range achi tarah naapna sab se mushkil hai kyunke scapula, trunk aur humerus sab shamil hotay hain. Landmarks aur woh tricks seekhein jo upper-limb readings ko repeatable banate hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll place the goniometer for shoulder flexion, abduction and rotation, elbow flexion and wrist extension, name the normal ranges and the common substitutions.
goal.ur: End tak aap shoulder flexion, abduction aur rotation, elbow flexion aur wrist extension ke liye goniometer rakhenge, normal ranges aur aam substitutions batayenge.

Control substitutions: knees bent for the back, palm up for abduction, towel under the humerus for the elbow, relaxed fingers for the wrist.

title: Sample Size and Power — Intuition First, Calculation Second

hook.en: "How many patients do I need?" is the first question every student researcher asks and the one most often answered with "about 30". A study that is too small cannot find real effects, and the ones it does find tend to be exaggerated. Learn the logic before you touch a calculator.
hook.ur: "Mujhe kitne mareez chahiye?" har talib-e-ilm muhaqqiq ka pehla sawal hai aur jis ka jawab aksar "takreeban 30" hota hai. Bohat chhota study asal asar nahi dhoondh sakta, aur jo dhoondhta hai woh aksar barha-chara hota hai. Calculator chhune se pehle mantiq seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain power in plain words, name the four things that decide sample size, perform a simple sample-size reasoning for a two-group trial, and know why "30 per group" is a poor rule.
goal.ur: End tak aap power ko saade alfaaz mein samjhayenge, sample size tay karne wali chaar cheezein batayenge, do-group trial ke liye saada sample-size mantiq karenge, aur jaanenge "30 per group" kyun kamzor qaida hai.

summaryEn: Power is the chance of detecting a real effect; sample size depends on effect size, variability, power and significance level.
Use the smallest important effect, not the hoped-for one, and add a margin for drop-outs.
Small studies are inconclusive and tend to overestimate effects; treat them as pilots.

next.title: Choosing a Statistical Test — A Simple Map for Therapists

title: Choosing a Statistical Test — A Simple Map for Therapists

hook.en: The scariest part of a thesis for many therapists is "which test do I use?". The answer is not memory, it is three questions: what kind of outcome, how many groups, and are they independent? Answer those and the test almost picks itself.
hook.ur: Bohat se therapists ke liye thesis ka sab se daravna hissa hai "kaun sa test istemal karun?". Jawab yaadasht nahi, teen sawal hain: nateeja kis qism ka, kitne groups, aur kya woh azaad hain? In ka jawab dein to test khud-ba-khud chun jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll classify an outcome (continuous, ordinal, categorical), choose between a parametric and a non-parametric test, pick the right test for two groups, three or more groups, paired data, categories and relationships, and know free software to run them.
goal.ur: End tak aap nateeje ki qism (mustaqil, ordinal, categorical) tay karenge, parametric aur non-parametric test mein se chunenge, do groups, teen ya zyada groups, paired data, categories aur rishton ke liye sahi test chunenge, aur unhein chalane ke liye muft software jaanenge.

summaryEn: Choose a test from three questions: outcome type, number of groups, and independent or paired data.
Use parametric tests for roughly normal continuous data and non-parametric tests for skewed, ordinal or very small samples.
Plot first, plan the test in advance and report effect sizes with intervals.

next.title: Regression Basics, Confounders and Adjustment

title: Regression Basics, Confounders and Adjustment

hook.en: A study says people who exercise live longer. But exercisers also smoke less, eat better and earn more. Regression is the tool that tries to separate these threads, and it is also easy to misuse. Learn what it can and cannot do.
hook.ur: Study kehti hai exercise karne walay zyada jeete hain. Lekin exercise karne walay cigarette kam peete, behtar khate aur zyada kamate hain. Regression woh aala hai jo in dhagon ko alag karne ki koshish karta hai, aur ismein ghalat istemal bhi aasaan hai. Seekhein yeh kya kar sakta hai aur kya nahi.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain what linear and logistic regression do, define a confounder and how adjustment works, read a regression coefficient or an odds ratio in plain words, and spot common errors such as too many variables and adjusting for the wrong thing.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke linear aur logistic regression kya karte hain, confounder aur adjustment ki tareef karenge, regression coefficient ya odds ratio saade alfaaz mein parhenge, aur aam ghaltiyan pehchanenge jaise bohat zyada variables aur ghalat cheez ko adjust karna.

summaryEn: Regression describes an outcome in relation to predictors, and adjustment accounts for measured confounders.
Do not adjust for mediators, do not overfit and remember unmeasured confounders remain.
Draw a causal diagram before modelling and use "associated with" for observational results.

next.title: Missing Data, Drop-outs and Bias

title: Missing Data, Drop-outs and Bias

hook.en: Every real study loses people: they move, get bored, get worse or get better and stop coming. The numbers that remain may tell a very different story from the full group. Learn why missing data matter, and what honest researchers do about them.
hook.ur: Har haqeeqi study mein log kam ho jate hain: shehar badal lete hain, bore ho jate hain, bigad jate hain ya theek ho kar aana band kar dete hain. Jo numbers bachte hain woh poore group se bilkul mukhtalif kahani suna sakte hain. Seekhein ke missing data kyun ahem hai aur imaandar muhaqqiq iska kya karte hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll tell three types of missing data (completely at random, at random, not at random), explain why drop-out can bias a trial, compare complete-case analysis, last observation carried forward and multiple imputation, and use sensitivity analysis.
goal.ur: End tak aap missing data ki teen qismein (bilkul random, random, random nahi) batayenge, samjhayenge ke drop-out trial ko kaise biased karta hai, complete-case analysis, last observation carried forward aur multiple imputation ka muqabla karenge, aur sensitivity analysis istemal karenge.

summaryEn: Drop-out can bias results, especially when people leave because of their outcome.
Compare methods: complete-case analysis, LOCF, multiple imputation and sensitivity analysis.
The best protection is prevention, with full reporting of numbers and reasons.

title: Subgroups, Multiple Testing and P-Hacking

hook.en: "The treatment did not work overall, but it worked in women over 50 with a history of knee pain on Tuesdays." Sound ridiculous? A chart of 20 tests will produce one "significant" result by chance alone. Learn how to spot findings that were dug out of the data, and how to avoid doing it.
hook.ur: "Ilaaj ne kul mila kar kaam nahi kiya, lekin 50 se zyada umar ki khawateen mein jinhein ghutne ke dard ki tareekh thi mangal ko kaam kiya." Bejaa lagta hai? 20 tests ka chart sirf ittifaq se ek "significant" nateeja paida kar dega. Seekhein ke data se khod kar nikaale gaye findings kaise pehchanein, aur khud aisa karne se kaise bachein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain why many tests make false positives likely, judge a subgroup claim with five questions, tell planned from post-hoc analyses, and name ways to avoid p-hacking such as pre-registration and correcting for multiple comparisons.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke bohat se tests jhoote positive ka imkaan kyun barhate hain, subgroup ke daawe ko paanch sawalon se parkhenge, planned ko post-hoc analyses se alag karenge, aur p-hacking se bachne ke tareeqe jaise pre-registration aur multiple comparisons ki correction batayenge.

summaryEn: Many tests make false positives likely: 20 tests at the 5 percent level give about a 64 percent chance of at least one.
Judge subgroup claims by whether they were planned, tested for interaction, counted, plausible and replicated.
Prevent p-hacking by pre-specifying one primary outcome and reporting everything you measured.

next.title: Bayesian Thinking for Clinicians

title: Bayesian Thinking for Clinicians

hook.en: You already think like a Bayesian. When a patient with a sore shoulder walks in, you have a first guess, you examine, and you update your guess. Bayesian thinking turns that instinct into a clear rule, and it protects you from some of the commonest mistakes in clinical reasoning.
hook.ur: Aap pehle se Bayesian ki tarah sochte hain. Jab kandhe ke dard wala mareez aata hai to aap ka pehla andaaza hota hai, aap muaina karte hain, aur andaaza update karte hain. Bayesian soch is jibillat ko saaf qaide mein badalti hai, aur clinical reasoning ki sab se aam ghaltiyon se bachati hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain prior, evidence and posterior probability in plain words, update a probability with a likelihood ratio, see why base rates matter, and recognise that a result means different things in different patients.
goal.ur: End tak aap prior, evidence aur posterior probability saade alfaaz mein samjhayenge, likelihood ratio se imkaan update karenge, dekhenge ke base rates kyun ahem hain, aur pehchanenge ke nateeja mukhtalif mareezon mein mukhtalif matlab rakhta hai.

summaryEn: Bayesian thinking updates a prior probability with evidence to give a posterior probability.
The same positive result means different things when the pre-test probability is high or low (base rates matter).
Low probability is not zero: keep red flags in mind and refer when a serious cause is plausible.

next.title: Meta-Analysis — Forest Plots, Heterogeneity and Publication Bias

title: Meta-Analysis — Forest Plots, Heterogeneity and Publication Bias

hook.en: A forest plot looks like an intimidating pile of squares and lines. It is actually the clearest picture in research: every study as a row, the result as a square, and the overall answer as a diamond. Learn to read it in thirty seconds, and to see when it should not be trusted.
hook.ur: Forest plot daraoni squares aur lakeeron ka dher lagta hai. Asal mein yeh research ki sab se saaf tasveer hai: har study ek qatar, nateeja ek square, aur kul jawab ek heera. Isay tees second mein parhna seekhein, aur dekhein kab is par bharosa nahi karna chahiye.

goal.en: By the end, you'll read a forest plot, explain pooled estimates and weighting, interpret I-squared as a measure of heterogeneity, choose between fixed-effect and random-effects reasoning, and recognise publication bias with a funnel plot.
goal.ur: End tak aap forest plot parhenge, pooled estimates aur weighting samjhayenge, I-squared ko heterogeneity ke naap ke taur par parhenge, fixed-effect aur random-effects mantiq mein se chunenge, aur funnel plot se publication bias pehchanenge.

summaryEn: A meta-analysis pools study results with weights; the forest plot shows each study and a pooled diamond.
High I-squared means studies differ a lot, so be careful with the average and look for reasons.
Publication bias can hide small negative studies; a meta-analysis is only as good as the studies and methods behind it.

next.title: Systematic and Scoping Reviews — PRISMA, Risk of Bias and GRADE

title: Systematic and Scoping Reviews — PRISMA, Risk of Bias and GRADE

hook.en: A narrative review is one expert's tour of the literature. A systematic review is a repeatable investigation with a written plan, a complete search and a fair judgement of every study. Learn how to tell them apart, and how to judge whether a review deserves your trust.
hook.ur: Narrative review ek maahir ka literature ka daura hai. Systematic review ek dohraya ja sakne wali tehqiq hai jis ka likha hua plan, mukammal search aur har study ka munsifana jaiza hota hai. Seekhein dono ko kaise alag karein, aur kaise parkhein ke review aap ke bharose ke qabil hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll distinguish narrative, systematic and scoping reviews, follow the PRISMA flow of a review, know what RoB 2 and ROBINS-I assess, and explain how GRADE rates the certainty of the evidence.
goal.ur: End tak aap narrative, systematic aur scoping reviews mein farq karenge, review ke PRISMA flow ko follow karenge, jaanenge RoB 2 aur ROBINS-I kya parakhte hain, aur samjhayenge ke GRADE saboot ki yaqeeniyat kaise rate karta hai.

title: Interpreting Patient-Reported Outcomes — Floor and Ceiling Effects, MCID by Anchor or Distribution

hook.en: A patient scores 85 out of 100 on a function questionnaire at the start, and 90 at the end. Success? Perhaps not: the questionnaire may have run out of room to show improvement. Learn how to read patient-reported scores with care.
hook.ur: Mareez function questionnaire par shuru mein 100 mein se 85 aur aakhir mein 90 score karta hai. Kamyabi? Shayad nahi: ho sakta hai questionnaire mein behtari dikhane ki jagah khatam ho gayi ho. Patient-reported scores ko ehtiyat se parhna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain floor and ceiling effects, tell an anchor-based MCID from a distribution-based one, judge individual change against group change, and choose a patient-reported measure that fits your patients.
goal.ur: End tak aap floor aur ceiling effects samjhayenge, anchor-based MCID ko distribution-based se alag karenge, infiradi tabdeeli ka group ki tabdeeli se muqabla karenge, aur apne mareezon ke liye munasib patient-reported measure chunenge.

title: Honest Graphs — Data Visualisation for Therapists

hook.en: A graph can tell the truth or tell a lie with exactly the same numbers. A bar chart with a cut-off axis makes a tiny change look huge; a bar of averages hides a whole crowd of patients. Learn to draw graphs that show what really happened, and to spot those that do not.
hook.ur: Graph wohi numbers ke saath sach ya jhoot bol sakta hai. Kata hua axis wala bar chart chhoti tabdeeli ko bara dikhata hai; averages ka bar mareezon ki poori bheed chhupa deta hai. Aise graphs banana seekhein jo dikhayein asal mein kya hua, aur woh pehchanein jo nahi dikhate.

goal.en: By the end, you'll choose a suitable chart for a given question, avoid misleading axes, show individual data instead of just averages, and spot the common tricks used to make results look bigger.
goal.ur: End tak aap diye gaye sawal ke liye munasib chart chunenge, gumrah karne wale axes se bachenge, sirf averages ke bajaye infiradi data dikhayenge, aur nateeje bara dikhane ki aam chaalein pehchanenge.

Do not hide non-responders or harm, and keep the design plain and readable.

hook.en: Most student projects fail before the first patient is recruited, because the question was too big, too vague or impossible to answer with the time and people available. A good question is half the research. FINER is a quick test to find out whether yours is one.
hook.ur: Zyada tar talba ke projects pehle mareez ke bharti hone se pehle hi nakam ho jate hain, kyunke sawal bohat bara, bohat mubham ya dastiyab waqt aur logon se jawab dene ke na-qabil tha. Achha sawal aadhi research hai. FINER ek tez test hai jo batata hai ke aap ka sawal achha hai ya nahi.

goal.en: By the end, you'll turn a topic into a focused question, test it against the FINER criteria (Feasible, Interesting, Novel, Ethical, Relevant), write aims and a hypothesis, and decide whether to narrow or drop an idea.

title: Writing a Research Proposal — Aims, Methods, Timeline and Budget

hook.en: A proposal is a promise: "this is what I will do, how, when and with what". A clear one gets approved, funded and finished. A vague one gets sent back. Learn the parts, and learn to write each in plain, honest language.
hook.ur: Proposal ek waada hai: "main yeh karunga, kaise, kab aur kis ke saath". Saaf proposal manzoor, funded aur mukammal hota hai. Mubham wapas bheja jata hai. Hissay seekhein, aur har ek saade, imaandar alfaaz mein likhna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll structure a proposal (title, background, aims, methods, analysis, ethics, timeline, budget, references), write a clear methods section, build a realistic timeline and budget, and avoid the usual reasons proposals are rejected.
goal.ur: End tak aap proposal ka dhancha banayenge (title, background, aims, methods, analysis, ethics, timeline, budget, references), saaf methods section likhenge, haqeeqat pasand timeline aur budget banayenge, aur proposals ke radd hone ki aam wajuhaat se bachenge.

Write methods specifically enough to repeat, and use a Gantt chart and itemised budget.
Be realistic and modest, plan for safety and use SPIRIT for trial protocols.

next.title: Research Ethics — Helsinki, Consent, Vulnerable Groups and Ethics Committees

title: Research Ethics — Helsinki, Consent, Vulnerable Groups and Ethics Committees

hook.en: Research asks people to give time, data and sometimes their health for knowledge that may only help others. That trust is sacred. Ethics is not paperwork; it is the promise that participants will be respected, protected and treated fairly. Learn the principles and the practical steps.
hook.ur: Research logon se waqt, data aur kabhi kabhi apni sehat ka sawal karti hai us ilm ke liye jo shayad sirf doosron ki madad kare. Yeh bharosa muqaddas hai. Ethics kaghazi karwai nahi; yeh waada hai ke shirkat karne walon ki izzat, hifazat aur munsifana salook hoga. Usool aur amali qadam seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll state the core principles (respect, beneficence, justice), explain informed consent, recognise vulnerable groups, describe data protection and the role of an ethics committee, and know what not to do.
goal.ur: End tak aap bunyadi usool (izzat, bhalai, insaaf) batayenge, batayi gayi razamandi samjhayenge, kamzor groups pehchanenge, data ki hifazat aur ethics committee ka kirdar bayan karenge, aur jaanenge kya nahi karna.

summaryEn: Research ethics rests on respect, beneficence and justice, set out in the Declaration of Helsinki.
Informed consent must be understood, voluntary and revocable; vulnerable groups need extra protection.
Get ethics approval before starting, protect data and report problems immediately.

next.title: Trial Registration, Pre-registration and Open Science

title: Trial Registration, Pre-registration and Open Science

hook.en: Imagine a runner who decides which race to enter after seeing the results. That is what happens when a study picks its main outcome after looking at the data. Registration is the public record of "this is what we said we would do, before we knew the results". It keeps research honest.
hook.ur: Sochein ek daurne wala jo nateeje dekhne ke baad tay karta hai ke kaun si daur mein hissa liya. Yehi hota hai jab study data dekhne ke baad apna asal nateeja chunti hai. Registration is baat ka aam record hai ke "hum ne nateeje jaanne se pehle kaha tha hum kya karenge". Yeh research ko imaandar rakhta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain why trials and many other studies should be registered, register a protocol on a public registry, describe pre-registration and registered reports, and share data and materials openly in a responsible way.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke trials aur bohat si doosri studies register kyun hone chahiyen, public registry par protocol register karenge, pre-registration aur registered reports bayan karenge, aur data aur materials zimmedari se khulle taur par share karenge.

summaryEn: Register trials publicly before the first participant, with a specific primary outcome and analysis plan.
Outcome switching and selective reporting are what registration is designed to expose.
Share data and materials openly when ethical, and always protect participants' privacy.

next.title: Research Data Management — Spreadsheets, Coding, Cleaning and Backup

title: Research Data Management — Spreadsheets, Coding, Cleaning and Backup

hook.en: The most common way to lose a research project is not a failed experiment. It is a spreadsheet with colours as data, a file named "final_final2", and one laptop that stops working. Good data habits are boring, and they save months.
hook.ur: Research project khone ka sab se aam tareeqa nakam tajruba nahi. Yeh woh spreadsheet hai jis mein rang data hain, "final_final2" naam ki file, aur ek laptop jo kaam karna band kar de. Achhi data ki aadatein bore karne wali hain, aur mahine bachati hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll set up a tidy data spreadsheet, write a simple data dictionary, clean and check data safely, follow the 3-2-1 backup rule, and protect participants' privacy.
goal.ur: End tak aap saaf data spreadsheet banayenge, saada data dictionary likhenge, data ko mehfooz tareeqe se saaf aur check karenge, 3-2-1 backup ka qaida follow karenge, aur shirkat karne walon ki nijiyat mehfooz rakhenge.

summaryEn: Keep data tidy: one row per participant, one column per variable, one value per cell, with participant codes and a data dictionary.
Keep raw data untouched, record every cleaning step and back up with the 3-2-1 rule.
Protect privacy with separate keys, encryption and secure storage.

next.title: The Reporting-Guidelines Map — CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, CARE, STARD and More

title: The Reporting-Guidelines Map — CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, CARE, STARD and More

hook.en: Every kind of study has a recipe for how it should be reported, written by international experts. Following it makes your paper clear, complete and much more likely to be accepted. Not knowing it is like cooking without the ingredient list. Here is the map.
hook.ur: Har qism ke study ki report ka ek nuskha hota hai jo beinul-aqwami maahireen ne likha. Iska follow karna aap ke paper ko saaf, mukammal aur manzoor hone ke zyada qabil banata hai. Ise na jaanna ajzaa ki list ke baghair pakane jaisa hai. Yeh naqsha hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll match a study design to its reporting guideline (CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, CARE, STARD, SRQR, COREQ and others), find guidelines through the EQUATOR Network and use the checklist before you write and before you submit.
goal.ur: End tak aap study design ko uski reporting guideline (CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, CARE, STARD, SRQR, COREQ aur doosri) se milayenge, EQUATOR Network se guidelines dhoondhenge aur likhne se pehle aur bhejne se pehle checklist istemal karenge.

summaryEn: Each study design has its own reporting guideline: CONSORT, STROBE, PRISMA, CARE, STARD, COREQ, SQUIRE and more.
Find them for free through the EQUATOR Network and use them while planning, not only at the end.
A guideline tells you what to report, not how good the study was; report harms as carefully as benefits.

next.title: Describing Interventions So Others Can Repeat Them (TIDieR)

title: Describing Interventions So Others Can Repeat Them (TIDieR)

hook.en: A trial says "exercise reduced pain". Which exercise? How many sets, how often, who supervised, and how was it progressed? Without these details, no therapist can repeat it, and the trial is almost useless in the clinic. TIDieR is the checklist that fixes this.
hook.ur: Trial kehta hai "exercise ne dard kam kiya". Kaun si exercise? Kitne sets, kitni baar, kis ki nigrani mein, aur progression kaise hui? In tafseelat ke baghair koi therapist isay dohra nahi sakta, aur trial clinic mein taqreeban bekaar hai. TIDieR woh checklist hai jo isay theek karti hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll use the 12-item TIDieR checklist to describe an intervention, spot poorly described treatments in papers, and write an intervention description that another therapist could follow.
goal.ur: End tak aap 12 items wali TIDieR checklist se intervention bayan karenge, papers mein kam tafseel wale ilaaj pehchanenge, aur aisi intervention ki tafseel likhenge jis par doosra therapist chal sake.

summaryEn: TIDieR's 12 items let readers repeat an intervention: name, why, what, who, how, where, dose, tailoring, changes and fidelity.
Always report the dose and describe the comparison treatment as well as the experimental one.
Write your own clinic protocols with TIDieR and include safety precautions and exclusions.

next.title: Writing IMRaD — From Abstract to Discussion

title: Writing IMRaD — From Abstract to Discussion

hook.en: Good research badly written is invisible. IMRaD (Introduction, Methods, Results and Discussion) is the standard shape of a scientific paper because it answers four questions in order: why did you do it, what did you do, what did you find and what does it mean? Learn to write each part in plain, honest language.
hook.ur: Achhi research jo kharab likhi gayi ho nazar nahi aati. IMRaD (Introduction, Methods, Results aur Discussion) science paper ki mayaari shakal hai kyunke yeh chaar sawalon ka tarteeb se jawab deti hai: aap ne kyun kiya, kya kiya, kya paya aur is ka kya matlab hai? Har hissa saade, imaandar alfaaz mein likhna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll structure a paper in IMRaD form, write a structured abstract, state results without interpreting them, build a balanced discussion with limitations, and revise for clarity.
goal.ur: End tak aap paper ko IMRaD shakal mein tarteeb denge, munazzam abstract likhenge, nateeje tafseer kiye baghair bayan karenge, hadon ke saath mutawazin discussion banayenge, aur wazahat ke liye nazar-e-saani karenge.

summaryEn: IMRaD answers four questions in order: why, how, what and so what.
Keep facts in Results and interpretation in Discussion, with honest limitations and conclusions that match the data.
Write methods and results first, the abstract last, in plain sentences, and report harms and uncertainties.

next.title: Choosing a Journal, Spotting Predatory Journals and Answering Reviewers

title: Choosing a Journal, Spotting Predatory Journals and Answering Reviewers

hook.en: You finished the paper. Now an email arrives: "We will publish your article in 48 hours for a small fee." Tempting, and a trap. Where you publish decides whether anyone trusts, finds and cites your work. Learn to choose well, and to handle peer review without taking it personally.
hook.ur: Aap ka paper mukammal ho gaya. Ab ek email aati hai: "Hum aap ka article 48 ghanton mein chhap denge, thori si fees par." Lubhane wali baat hai, aur jaal bhi. Aap kahan chhapte hain yeh tay karta hai ke koi aap ke kaam par bharosa karega, dhoondhe ga aur hawala dega ya nahi. Achha chunna seekhein, aur peer review ko zaati liye baghair sambhalna.

goal.en: By the end, you'll shortlist suitable journals, check a journal with a simple checklist, recognise predatory journals and fake invitations, understand how peer review works, and write a calm point-by-point reply to reviewers.
goal.ur: End tak aap munasib journals ki fehrist banayenge, saade checklist se journal jaanchenge, predatory journals aur jhoote dawat-name pehchanenge, peer review ka amal samjhenge, aur reviewers ko pur-sukoon point-by-point jawab likhenge.

summaryEn: Choose a journal that fits, is truly indexed, and has a clear peer review process and costs.
Predatory journals promise speed and guaranteed acceptance, mislead about indexing, and take fees without real review.
Answer reviewers calmly, point by point, and see rejection as free advice.

next.title: Posters and Conference Talks That People Actually Remember

title: Posters and Conference Talks That People Actually Remember

hook.en: At a conference, people walk past a poster in about ten seconds, and a talk is forgotten by lunch unless it has one clear idea. A poster is an advertisement for your work, and a talk is a conversation with a room. Learn to design both for a tired, busy human being.
hook.ur: Conference mein log poster ke saamne se takreeban das second mein guzar jate hain, aur talk dopahar tak bhula di jati hai jab tak us mein ek saaf khayal na ho. Poster aap ke kaam ka ishtihaar hai, aur talk ek kamray se baat cheet. Dono ko thake, masroof insaan ke liye design karna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll structure a poster around three messages, design it for reading from two metres, plan a 10-minute talk with one idea per slide, rehearse it, and handle questions calmly.
goal.ur: End tak aap poster ko teen paighamat par tarteeb denge, do meter se parhne ke liye design karenge, ek slide ek khayal ke saath 10 minute ki talk plan karenge, mashq karenge, aur sawalon ko pur-sukoon sambhalenge.

summaryEn: Build a poster or talk around one message, with a big figure and very few words.
Plan about one slide per minute, make titles state the finding, and practise aloud with a timer.
Protect patients' identity, declare conflicts and state limits calmly.

next.title: Manual Muscle Testing — The 0 to 5 Scale Without Guesswork

title: Manual Muscle Testing — The 0 to 5 Scale Without Guesswork

hook.en: Grade 3 is the line between a muscle that can lift the limb and one that cannot. Learn the scale, the gravity-decides rule and how to resist without guessing.
hook.ur: Grade 3 us muscle ke beech ki line hai jo limb ko utha sakta hai aur jo nahi utha sakta. Scale, gravity-decides ka qaida aur bina andaza lagaye resist karna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll grade strength 0–5 for any muscle, choose the correct gravity position, give resistance at the right place and time, and record the result clearly.
goal.ur: End tak aap kisi bhi muscle ki taqat 0–5 grade karenge, sahi gravity position chunenge, sahi jagah aur sahi waqt par resistance denge aur result saaf likhenge.

summaryEn: 0 none, 1 flicker, 2 full range gravity-eliminated, 3 full range against gravity, 4 against moderate resistance, 5 against maximal resistance.
Use the 8 steps: explain, position, stabilise, show, test grade 3 then resist slowly at the distal end, grade and compare, document.

next.title: Finishing Your Thesis and Working With Your Supervisor

title: Finishing Your Thesis and Working With Your Supervisor

hook.en: Most theses are not late because of hard science. They are late because of unclear plans, silent weeks and a draft nobody has read. A thesis is a project, and a supervisor is a partner in it. Learn how to manage both, kindly and firmly.
hook.ur: Zyada tar theses mushkil science ki wajah se late nahi hoti. Woh ghair-wazeh plans, khamosh haftoon aur aise draft ki wajah se late hoti hain jo kisi ne parha hi nahi. Thesis ek project hai, aur supervisor us mein shareek. Dono ko narmi aur mazbooti se sambhalna seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll plan a thesis backwards from the deadline, run useful supervisor meetings, write a little every week, handle citations and backups, agree authorship early, and prepare for the viva.
goal.ur: End tak aap deadline se peechay ki taraf thesis ka plan banayenge, supervisor ki mufeed mulaqatein chalayenge, har haftay thora likhenge, hawale aur backups sambhalenge, musannifi pehle tay karenge, aur viva ki tayyari karenge.

summaryEn: Plan the thesis backwards from the deadline, write a little every week and keep three backups.
Run supervisor meetings with an agenda and a written summary, and agree authorship early in writing.
Use a reference manager, never fabricate data, and prepare for the viva as a conversation.

next.title: MMT of the Shoulder Girdle and Arm — Catching the Cheats

title: MMT of the Shoulder Girdle and Arm — Catching the Cheats

hook.en: A weak muscle always borrows help from a stronger neighbour. Learn to spot the shrug, the lean and the swing so a "4/5" really means a 4/5 in the muscle you meant to test.
hook.ur: Kamzor muscle hamesha mazboot padosi se madad leta hai. Shrug, lean aur swing pehchanna seekhein taake “4/5” ka matlab wohi muscle ho jisay aap test karna chahte the.

goal.en: By the end, you'll test the serratus anterior, trapezius, rhomboids, deltoid and elbow flexors and extensors correctly and name the substitution for each.
goal.ur: End tak aap serratus anterior, trapezius, rhomboids, deltoid aur elbow flexors aur extensors sahi test karenge aur har ek ki substitution batayenge.

summaryEn: Every movement has helpers; watch the whole body and use the standard position that blocks the cheat.
Classic cheats: shrug for shoulder lift, trunk lean, wrist flexors for elbow flexion, tenodesis in the hand, winging for serratus anterior.

next.title: MMT of the Hip, Knee and Ankle — Gluteals, Quadriceps and the Calf

title: MMT of the Hip, Knee and Ankle — Gluteals, Quadriceps and the Calf

hook.en: The legs are the strongest muscles in the body, so the standard hands-on test often says "5/5" when real strength is missing. Learn the correct positions, the Trendelenburg link and why the calf is tested by heel raises.
hook.ur: Taangein jism ke sab se mazboot muscles hain, is liye standard hands-on test aksar “5/5” kehta hai jab asal taqat kam hoti hai. Sahi positions, Trendelenburg ka link aur calf heel raises se kyun test hota hai seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll test gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, quadriceps and the calf with correct positions and resistance, name the substitution for each and use functional tests for the big muscles.
goal.ur: End tak aap gluteus medius, gluteus maximus, quadriceps aur calf ko sahi position aur resistance se test karenge, har ek ki substitution batayenge aur bare muscles ke liye functional tests use karenge.

hook.en: "Tight hamstrings" is the most over-used diagnosis in physiotherapy. Learn to test muscle length so carefully that you know which muscle is short, which compensation is hiding it and when stretching is the wrong answer.
hook.ur: “Tight hamstrings” physiotherapy ki sab se zyada istemal hone wali tashkhees hai. Muscle length itni ehtiyat se test karna seekhein ke aap ko pata ho kaun sa muscle chhota hai, kaun si compensation usay chhupa rahi hai aur stretching kab ghalat jawab hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll perform the modified Thomas, Ely, Ober, passive straight-leg raise and gastrocnemius–soleus tests, name the normal finding and the compensation for each, and decide when stretching is justified.
goal.ur: End tak aap modified Thomas, Ely, Ober, passive straight-leg raise aur gastrocnemius–soleus tests karenge, har ek ki normal finding aur compensation batayenge, aur tay karenge ke stretching kab durust hai.

summaryEn: Move passively to the first firm resistance or compensation; two-joint muscles need both joints in position, one-joint muscles need only one.

hook.en: A centimetre decides whether a leg is truly short, whether the pelvis is tilted or whether the knee is swollen. Learn tape-measure rules that make every number repeatable.

hook.en: Hip and groin pain has many causes: the joint, the labrum, a tendon, a stress fracture, the spine, even the abdomen. Learn a clear order of examination and the signs that mean "do not just treat".
hook.ur: Hip aur groin ke dard ki bohat si wajuhat hain: joint, labrum, tendon, stress fracture, spine, hatta ke pait. Examination ki saaf tartib seekhein aur woh nishaniyan jin ka matlab hai "sirf treat na karein".

hook.en: Walking for six minutes tells you more about a patient's daily life than many lab tests. Learn to run the test exactly the same way every time, watch the oxygen level and breathlessness, and know when to stop.
hook.ur: Chhe minute chalna rozmarra zindagi ke baare mein bohat si lab tests se zyada batata hai. Test ko har baar bilkul ek hi tareeqe se karna, oxygen aur saans ki tangi dekhna aur rukne ka waqt jaanna seekhein.

hook.en: Experts are not smarter, they think in a different order: they form early ideas, test them, look for what does not fit and know their own thinking traps. Learn that order and the common errors.

title: The Pelvic Floor — Leaks, Pregnancy and Life After Childbirth

hook.en: Leaking urine after a cough or a jump is common but not normal, and many women never ask for help. Learn what the pelvic floor does, how to train it properly and when to refer.
hook.ur: Khansi ya chhalang par peshab ka nikalna aam hai magar normal nahi, aur bohat si khawateen madad nahi maangtin. Seekhein ke pelvic floor kya karta hai, ise sahi tareeqe se kaise train karein aur kab refer karein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain the pelvic floor in plain words, teach a correct contraction with a gradual programme, adapt it for pregnancy and the weeks after birth, and recognise signs that need a doctor.
goal.ur: End tak aap pelvic floor saada alfaz mein samjhayenge, sahi contraction aur darje war programme sikhayenge, ise hamal aur paidaish ke baad ke haftay ke liye adjust karenge, aur woh nishaniyan pehchanenge jin ke liye doctor chahiye.

hook.en: One in three older adults falls each year, and a fall can end independence. Exercise is the best-proven way to prevent falls. Learn to screen, to choose the right exercise and to build it into daily life.
hook.ur: Har saal teen mein se ek buzurg girta hai, aur ek girna khud mukhtari khatam kar sakta hai. Exercise girne se bachao ka sab se behtar sabit shuda tareeqa hai. Screen karna, sahi exercise chunna aur isay rozmarra zindagi mein shamil karna seekhein.

title: Osteoporosis — Exercising Safely to Protect Bones

hook.en: Bones respond to load, even in older age. Learn which exercises build and protect bone, which movements to avoid after a spinal fracture and how to keep a person with osteoporosis strong and confident.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain osteoporosis simply, screen for spinal fracture, and prescribe weight-bearing, resistance and balance exercise while avoiding loaded forward bending and twisting.
goal.ur: End tak aap osteoporosis saada alfaz mein samjhayenge, spine fracture ki screening karenge, aur wazan uthane wali, resistance aur balance exercise dein ge jabke loaded aage jhukne aur ghoomne se bachayenge.

hook.en: A knee replacement removes the pain, but the muscles and movement must be rebuilt. Learn the stages of rehab, the goals that matter and the warning signs you must never miss.

goal.en: By the end, you'll plan rehab from day one to the return to full activity, set range and strength goals, manage swelling and pain, and recognise infection, a clot or a stiff knee that needs the surgeon.

goal.en: By the end, you'll check a trial for random allocation, concealment, blinding, dropouts and outcome reporting, read a mean difference with its confidence interval, and decide whether the result is both believable and important.
goal.ur: End tak aap trial mein random allocation, concealment, blinding, dropouts aur outcome reporting check karenge, mean difference ko confidence interval ke saath parhenge, aur faisla karenge ke nateeja qabil-e-yaqeen bhi hai aur ahem bhi.

summaryEn: Check how groups were formed (random and hidden), blinding and follow-up, and whether the main outcome was reported as planned.

title: Outcome Measures — Is the Change Real and Does It Matter?

hook.en: A patient's score went from 20 to 18. Is that progress, or noise? Learn to choose an outcome measure, read a change score and use the minimal important change so you can show patients and others that treatment is working.
hook.ur: Mareez ka score 20 se 18 hua. Kya yeh progress hai ya shor? Outcome measure chunna, change score parhna aur minimal important change istemal karna seekhein taake aap mareezon aur doosron ko dikha sakein ke ilaj kaam kar raha hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll choose a validated measure for pain, disability or function, record a baseline, calculate change, and judge it against measurement error and the minimal important change.
goal.ur: End tak aap dard, disability ya function ke liye validated measure chunenge, baseline likhenge, change nikalenge, aur use measurement error aur minimal important change se parkhenge.

summaryEn: Choose a valid, reliable, responsive measure with the patient, record a baseline and repeat it in the same way.
A change is real if it is bigger than the measurement error and meaningful if it is bigger than the minimal important change.

next.title: Cardiac Rehabilitation — Exercising Safely After a Heart Event

title: Cardiac Rehabilitation — Exercising Safely After a Heart Event

hook.en: After a heart attack or bypass, patients fear exercise. Yet supervised, graded exercise lowers deaths and readmissions. Learn the phases, how hard to push and when to stop.
hook.ur: Dil ke daure ya bypass ke baad mareez exercise se darte hain. Phir bhi nigrani wali, darje war exercise mauton aur dobara daakhilon ko kam karti hai. Marahil, kitna zor lagana hai aur kab rukna hai seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll describe the phases of cardiac rehabilitation, screen before exercise, set intensity with heart rate and the Borg scale, and recognise stop signs and emergencies.
goal.ur: End tak aap cardiac rehabilitation ke marahil bayan karenge, exercise se pehle screening karenge, heart rate aur Borg scale se shiddat tay karenge, aur rukne ki nishaniyan aur emergencies pehchanenge.

summaryEn: Cardiac rehabilitation combines exercise, education and risk-factor control, in early, outpatient and maintenance phases.

Know the stop signs and emergencies, and build the patient's confidence as well as fitness.

next.title: Heat and Cold — What They Really Do and When to Avoid Them

title: Heat and Cold — What They Really Do and When to Avoid Them

hook.en: Hot packs and ice are the most used treatments in clinics and homes, yet many people use them wrongly. Learn what each really does, what the evidence says and the safety rules that protect the skin.
hook.ur: Garam packs aur barf clinics aur gharon mein sab se zyada istemal hone wale ilaj hain, phir bhi bohat se log inhein ghalat istemal karte hain. Seekhein har ek asal mein kya karta hai, evidence kya kehta hai aur jild ki hifazat ke safety usool.

goal.en: By the end, you'll choose heat or cold for a given problem, apply each safely with time limits and skin checks, explain the PEACE and LOVE approach to soft-tissue injury and know when to avoid both.
goal.ur: End tak aap kisi masle ke liye garmi ya sardi chunenge, har ek ko waqt ki hadd aur jild ki jaanch ke saath mehfooz tareeqe se lagayenge, soft-tissue chot ke liye PEACE aur LOVE approach samjhayenge aur jaanenge ke dono se kab bachna hai.

summaryEn: Heat suits stiff, non-swollen tissue and cold gives short-term pain relief; both are adjuncts that help movement, not cures.
Apply with a barrier for 10 to 20 minutes, check the skin, and avoid both where sensation or circulation is poor.
For early soft-tissue injury, use PEACE and LOVE: protect first, then load early and progress.

next.title: Passing the OSCE and Viva — A Method, Not Luck

title: Passing the OSCE and Viva — A Method, Not Luck

hook.en: OSCE and viva exams reward a clear routine under time pressure. Learn how stations are marked, a simple structure for every station and how to practise so that you stay calm.
hook.ur: OSCE aur viva exams waqt ke dabao mein saaf routine ko inaam dete hain. Seekhein stations kaise marks hote hain, har station ke liye saada dhancha aur practice kaise karein taake aap pur-sukoon rahein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll read a station task quickly, follow a safe routine (introduce, consent, expose, examine, explain), manage the clock, and practise with a partner using a checklist.
goal.ur: End tak aap station ka task jaldi parhenge, mehfooz routine (taaruf, razamandi, expose, examine, explain) par chalenge, ghari sambhalenge, aur partner ke saath checklist se practice karenge.

summaryEn: OSCE stations are marked on checklists of actions, communication and safety, so a routine earns reliable marks.
Use the same routine at every station: read, introduce, consent, expose, examine, explain, and watch the clock.
If you forget a step, say so and carry on; practise aloud with a partner, a stopwatch and a checklist.

next.title: Writing Clear Clinical Notes — SOAP, Consent and Safe Records

title: Writing Clear Clinical Notes — SOAP, Consent and Safe Records

hook.en: Good notes protect patients, colleagues and you. Learn a simple SOAP structure, what must always be recorded and the habits that make a note useful a month later.
hook.ur: Achhe notes mareezon, saathiyon aur aap ki hifazat karte hain. Saada SOAP dhancha, jo hamesha likhna hai aur woh aadatein seekhein jo note ko ek mahine baad bhi mufeed banati hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll write a SOAP note with measurable findings and a clear plan, record consent, safety screening and advice, and keep patient information private.
goal.ur: End tak aap naapne ke qabil findings aur saaf plan ke saath SOAP note likhenge, razamandi, hifazati screening aur mashwara likhenge, aur mareez ki maloomat ko mehfooz rakhenge.

summaryEn: A SOAP note records what the patient says (subjective), what you measure (objective), your reasoning (assessment) and your plan.
Use measurable findings, record consent, safety screening, advice and the review date, and sign and date every entry.
Never alter old entries or write opinions as facts, and keep patient information private.

next.title: Flat Feet, In-Toeing and Bow Legs in Children — When to Reassure and When to Refer

title: Flat Feet, In-Toeing and Bow Legs in Children — When to Reassure and When to Refer

hook.en: Parents worry when a child's feet turn in or have no arch. Most of these are normal stages of growth. Learn how to examine, reassure with confidence and spot the few that need a specialist.
hook.ur: Walidain pareshan hote hain jab bachay ke pair andar ki taraf murte hain ya arch nahi hota. Zyada tar yeh nashonuma ke normal marahil hain. Examine karna, itminan se tasalli dena aur woh chand pehchanna seekhein jin ke liye specialist chahiye.

goal.en: By the end, you'll tell a flexible flat foot, in-toeing and physiological bow legs from conditions that need referral, perform simple screening and give clear advice to parents.
goal.ur: End tak aap flexible flat foot, in-toeing aur physiological bow legs ko un halaton se alag karenge jin ke liye referral chahiye, saada screening karenge aur walidain ko saaf mashwara denge.

summaryEn: Flat feet, in-toeing and bow legs are usually normal variants when painless, symmetrical and flexible.
Examine the arch on tiptoe, the rotation (hip, thigh-foot angle) and walking, and reassure with a clear explanation.
Refer for pain, limp, stiffness, one-sided findings, rapid change or a rigid foot; do not prescribe insoles for normal feet.

title: Breathlessness — Positions, Pacing and Breathing Control

hook.en: Breathlessness is frightening, and fear makes it worse. Learn the simple positions, pacing and breathing techniques that patients can use at home to take back control.
hook.ur: Saans ki tangi dara deti hai, aur dar usay barhata hai. Woh saadi positions, pacing aur saans ke tareeqe seekhein jo mareez ghar par istemal karke qaboo wapas pa sakte hain.

goal.en: By the end, you'll teach pursed-lip breathing, breathing control, recovery positions, pacing and a hand-held fan, set a simple action plan and recognise when breathlessness is an emergency.
goal.ur: End tak aap pursed-lip breathing, breathing control, recovery positions, pacing aur hath ka pankha sikhayenge, saada action plan banayenge aur pehchanenge ke saans ki tangi kab emergency hai.

summaryEn: Breathlessness often brings panic that makes it worse; self-management breaks the cycle with positions, pursed-lip breathing, pacing and a fan.

next.title: Returning to Exercise After Childbirth — Gradual, Safe and Individual

title: Returning to Exercise After Childbirth — Gradual, Safe and Individual

hook.en: New mothers get conflicting advice about when and how to exercise again. Learn a safe, stepwise plan, how to check the abdominal wall and pelvic floor and which signs mean wait.
hook.ur: Nai mayon ko kab aur kaise dobara exercise karni hai is par mukhtalif mashware milte hain. Mehfooz, marhale war plan, pait ki deewar aur pelvic floor check karna aur woh nishaniyan seekhein jin ka matlab hai intezaar karein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll assess a postnatal woman, advise on early walking and pelvic floor work, progress strength and impact in stages, and handle abdominal separation, scars and leaking with confidence.
goal.ur: End tak aap postnatal aurat ki assessment karenge, jaldi chalne aur pelvic floor ke kaam par mashwara denge, taaqat aur impact marhalon mein barhayenge, aur pait ki alag hone, scar aur leaking ko aitemad se sambhalenge.

summaryEn: Start gentle movement soon after birth; return to impact depends on readiness (no leaking, heaviness or pain), not on a fixed date.
Build pelvic floor and strength in stages, and test hops and run-walk intervals before running; an abdominal gap is common and often narrows.
Watch for bleeding, fever, calf pain, a bulge or low mood and refer promptly.

title: Reading a Bone X-ray — A Safe Routine for Fractures and Joints

hook.ur: X-ray report faisla karti hai ke aap ilaj karein, refer karein ya intezaar. Seekhein saada X-ray kya dikhata hai, use dekhne ki saadi routine, aur physiotherapist ke taur par aap kya keh sakte hain aur kya nahi.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain what an X-ray shows, use an ABCS routine to look at a bone X-ray, read the words in a report (fracture, displacement, joint space, osteophyte) and know when a normal X-ray still needs follow-up.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke X-ray kya dikhata hai, hadi X-ray dekhne ke liye ABCS routine istemal karenge, report ke alfaz (fracture, displacement, joint space, osteophyte) parhenge aur jaanenge ke normal X-ray ke baad bhi follow-up kab chahiye.

summaryEn: An X-ray shows density: bone is white, air black and soft tissue grey; always ask for two views including the joint above and below.

goal.ur: End tak aap chest X-ray ki quality check karenge, ABCDE routine follow karenge, report mein consolidation, collapse, effusion aur pneumothorax pehchanenge aur mehfooz positions aur techniques chunenge.

hook.ur: CT scan chand minute mein tafseeli 3D tasveer deta hai aur trauma, seene aur sar ke masail mein aam hai. Seekhein yeh kya achha dikhata hai, MRI se kaise mukhtalif hai aur report ko ehtiyat se kaise parhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain how CT works, say what it shows best, compare it with X-ray and MRI, understand windows, contrast and radiation, and read key report terms safely.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke CT kaise kaam karta hai, kya sab se achha dikhata hai, isay X-ray aur MRI se muqabil karenge, windows, contrast aur radiation samjhenge, aur report ke aham alfaz mehfooz tareeqe se parhenge.

summaryEn: CT builds slices from many X-ray pictures; it is fast and shows bone, bleeding and lungs well, but shows soft tissue less well than MRI and uses radiation.

hook.en: "Disc bulge", "degenerative changes", "tear". MRI reports can frighten patients, and many findings are common in people with no pain. Learn how MRI works, how to read an image's brightness and how to put a report in perspective.

next.title: Reading an ECG — Rate, Rhythm and the Signs That Mean Stop

title: Reading an ECG — Rate, Rhythm and the Signs That Mean Stop

hook.en: In cardiac and ICU rehabilitation you will see ECG strips and monitors every day. Learn a five-step routine, the common rhythms and the changes that mean you stop exercise and call for help.
hook.ur: Cardiac aur ICU rehabilitation mein aap rozana ECG strips aur monitors dekhenge. Paanch qadam ki routine, aam rhythms aur woh tabdeeliyan seekhein jin ka matlab hai exercise rok kar madad bulayein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll find the heart rate on a strip, decide if the rhythm is regular and sinus, recognise atrial fibrillation, ST elevation and wide-complex tachycardia, and state when to stop and escalate.
goal.ur: End tak aap strip par heart rate nikalenge, faisla karenge ke rhythm regular aur sinus hai ya nahi, atrial fibrillation, ST elevation aur wide-complex tachycardia pehchanenge, aur batayenge ke kab rukna aur escalate karna hai.

summaryEn: An ECG shows the heart's electrical activity: P wave, QRS and T wave; use five steps: rate, rhythm, P waves, QRS width and ST segment.

hook.en: A blood test can tell you that a patient is anaemic, infected, dehydrated, bleeding or on blood thinners, all of which change what exercise is safe. Learn the common tests and how to use them.

goal.en: By the end, you'll read a basic lab report, know the usual ranges and the meaning of the common tests (blood count, inflammation, sugar, kidney and salts, clotting) and decide when a result limits exercise or needs the doctor.
goal.ur: End tak aap basic lab report parhenge, aam ranges aur aam tests (blood count, sozish, sugar, gurda aur namkiyat, jamne) ka matlab jaanenge aur faisla karenge ke nateeja kab exercise ko mehdood karta hai ya doctor chahiye.

next.title: Diagnostic Ultrasound — Tendons, Muscles, Fluid and Veins

title: Diagnostic Ultrasound — Tendons, Muscles, Fluid and Veins

hook.en: Ultrasound uses sound, not radiation, and can show a tendon move in real time. Learn what it shows well, how to read the words in a report and when it is the right first test.
hook.ur: Ultrasound radiation nahi, awaaz istemal karta hai, aur tendon ko harkat karte hue dikha sakta hai. Seekhein yeh kya achha dikhata hai, report ke alfaz kaise parhein aur yeh pehla sahi test kab hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll explain how ultrasound works, describe bright and dark (echogenic and anechoic) structures, say when ultrasound beats MRI or X-ray, and recognise report terms for tendon tears, tendinopathy, fluid and a clot in a vein.
goal.ur: End tak aap samjhayenge ke ultrasound kaise kaam karta hai, roshan aur kaali (echogenic aur anechoic) structures batayenge, kehenge ke ultrasound MRI ya X-ray se kab behtar hai, aur tendon tears, tendinopathy, fluid aur nas mein clot ke report alfaz pehchanenge.
