hook.en: Five times a day, millions of people stand, bow, kneel and sit on their heels. For a patient with knee, hip or back pain, or after surgery, prayer can become a source of fear. A physiotherapist who understands the movements, and respects the practice, can help the patient pray in comfort and safely.
hook.ur: Din mein paanch baar karoron log khade hote hain, jhukte hain, ghutnon ke bal baithte hain aur eriyon par baithte hain. Ghutne, hip ya kamar ke dard wale ya surgery ke baad mareez ke liye namaaz dar ka sabab ban sakti hai. Jo physiotherapist in harkaton ko samjhe aur is amal ka ehtram kare woh mareez ko aaram aur hifazat se namaaz parhne mein madad kar sakta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll break the prayer into its joint movements, spot which ones strain a painful knee, hip or back, offer practical options while the patient decides with their own scholar, and speak respectfully.
goal.ur: End tak aap namaaz ko uski joint ki harkaton mein todenge, pehchanenge ke kaun si harkat dukhte ghutne, hip ya kamar par bojh dalti hai, amali options dein ge jabke mareez apne aalim se faisla kare, aur izzat ke saath baat karenge.

summaryEn: Break prayer into joint movements, find the one that hurts, and keep the plan respectful: you offer options, the patient decides with their scholar.

next.title: Strength Training for Patients — Load, Effort and Safe Progression

title: Strength Training for Patients — Load, Effort and Safe Progression

hook.en: Strength is the most powerful tool in rehabilitation, and the one most often under-dosed. Patients stay on the same light weights for months, or jump the load and flare up. Learn a simple way to set the effort, progress step by step and keep pain on your side.
hook.ur: Taqat rehab ka sab se taqatwar hathiyar hai, aur sab se zyada kam dose mein diya jane wala bhi. Mareez mahinon ek hi halke wazan par rehte hain, ya load ek dam barha kar dard bhara dete hain. Effort tay karne, qadam ba qadam aage barhne aur dard ko apne saath rakhne ka saada tareeqa seekhein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll choose a starting load by effort, use reps in reserve (RIR) and rate of perceived exertion (RPE), progress one variable at a time with the two-for-two rule, manage pain with a simple traffic-light, and explain to a patient why strength comes before size.
goal.ur: End tak aap effort se shuruaati load chunenge, reps in reserve (RIR) aur rate of perceived exertion (RPE) istemal karenge, do-ke-do rule se ek waqt mein ek variable aage barhayenge, saade traffic-light se dard sambhalenge, aur mareez ko samjhayenge ke taqat size se pehle kyun aati hai.

summaryEn: Progress strength by effort: start with three to four reps left, change one variable at a time, and raise the load with the two-for-two rule.
Mild pain that settles within hours and is not worse the next day is usually acceptable; sharp or growing pain means stop and change something.
Early strength gains are nervous-system gains; muscle size follows later, so explain this to patients.

title: Critical Appraisal in Ten Minutes — Is This Trial Worth Believing?

hook.en: Every week someone says, "A new study proves this treatment works." Sometimes it does. Often it does not. You do not need a statistics degree to tell the difference. You need ten minutes and six questions.
hook.ur: Har haftay koi kehta hai, "Nayi study ne sabit kar diya ke yeh ilaaj kaam karta hai." Kabhi karta hai. Aksar nahi. Farq pehchanne ke liye statistics ki degree nahi chahiye. Das minute aur chhe sawal chahiye.

goal.en: By the end, you'll appraise a treatment trial with six questions (RACE-C), read a confidence interval against a clinically important change, spot spin in an abstract, and decide whether a trial should change your practice.
goal.ur: End tak aap chhe sawalon (RACE-C) se ilaaj ke trial ko parkhenge, confidence interval ko clinically ahem tabdeeli ke mukable mein parhenge, abstract mein spin pehchanenge, aur tay karenge ke trial aap ki practice badle ya nahi.

summaryEn: Appraise with three questions: is it valid, what did it find, does it apply to my patient.
Use RACE-C to check the methods, and compare the confidence interval with the smallest change that matters to patients.
Read beyond the abstract, watch for spin, and never change practice on one small trial.

next.title: The Limping Child — Paediatric Orthopaedics, Clubfoot and Red Flags

title: The Limping Child — Paediatric Orthopaedics, Clubfoot and Red Flags

hook.en: A child is not a small adult. A limp in a four-year-old and a limp in a thirteen-year-old mean very different things, and a few of them cannot wait. Learn to ask the age first, then sort the limp into safe, watch and urgent.
hook.ur: Bacha chhota bara nahi hota. Chaar saal ke bache ka langar aur terah saal ke bache ka langar bilkul mukhtalif matlab rakhte hain, aur kuch intezar nahi kar sakte. Pehle umar poochhna seekhein, phir langar ko mehfooz, nigrani aur urgent mein baantein.

goal.en: By the end, you'll sort a limping child by age, spot the urgent causes (septic arthritis, slipped capital femoral epiphysis), describe the Ponseti approach to clubfoot, recognise developmental hip dysplasia and Duchenne signs, and counsel Pakistani families clearly.
goal.ur: End tak aap langarte bache ko umar se chhantenge, urgent wajuhaat (septic arthritis, slipped capital femoral epiphysis) pehchanenge, clubfoot ke Ponseti tareeqe ko bayan karenge, developmental hip dysplasia aur Duchenne ki nishaniyan pehchanenge, aur Pakistani khandanon ko saaf samjhayenge.

summaryEn: In a limping child, ask the age, check weight-bearing and fever, and always examine the hip first.
Urgent causes such as septic arthritis and slipped capital femoral epiphysis cannot wait; refer on the same day.
Clubfoot is treated early with Ponseti casting and a brace; developmental hip dysplasia needs early scanning and a harness.

next.title: Pelvic Floor for Everyone — Leaks, Prolapse and Diastasis Recti

title: Pelvic Floor for Everyone — Leaks, Prolapse and Diastasis Recti

hook.en: Roughly one in three women leaks urine at some point, and many men leak after prostate surgery, yet most never tell anyone. In Pakistan shame is the real barrier. A calm, private, evidence-based conversation can change a life.
hook.ur: Takreeban teen mein se ek aurat kabhi na kabhi peshab ka rishaw mehsoos karti hai, aur bohat se mard prostate surgery ke baad, lekin zyada tar kisi ko nahi batate. Pakistan mein sharam asal rukawat hai. Pur-sukoon, nijji, saboot par mabni baat zindagi badal sakti hai.

goal.ur: End tak aap pelvic floor ka kaam samjhayenge, aam masail (stress aur urge rishaw, prolapse, diastasis recti, prostate surgery ke baad mard) ke naam batayenge, sahi pelvic floor contraction sikhayenge, jaanenge ke Kegels kab NAHI sikhane, aur red flags pehchanenge.

summaryEn: The pelvic floor can be too weak or too tight; check which before choosing exercise.
Pelvic floor muscle training is first-line for stress leakage and works best when supervised and taught correctly.
Make it private and consensual, watch for red flags such as cauda equina, and reassure that diastasis recti is treatable with strength and function.

next.title: Why Evidence-Based Practice? Three Legs of the Stool

title: Why Evidence-Based Practice? Three Legs of the Stool

hook.en: "We have always done it this way" has hurt patients before. But "the study says so" can hurt too, if it ignores the person in front of you. Evidence-based practice is not a cookbook. It is a three-legged stool, and a stool with one leg falls over.
hook.ur: "Hum hamesha aise hi karte aaye hain" ne pehle bhi mareezon ko nuqsan pohanchaya hai. Lekin "study kehti hai" bhi nuqsan de sakta hai, agar saamne baithe insaan ko nazar-andaaz kare. Evidence-based practice recipe book nahi. Yeh teen taangon wali kursi hai, aur ek taang wali kursi gir jati hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll name the three legs of evidence-based practice, explain what happens when one leg is missing, and show how to bring research, experience and patient values into one decision.
goal.ur: End tak aap evidence-based practice ki teen taangein batayenge, samjhayenge ke ek taang na ho to kya hota hai, aur research, tajurba aur mareez ki values ko ek faisle mein jorna dikhayenge.

summaryEn: EBP combines best research, clinical experience and patient values; no leg works alone.
Use the five steps: ask, acquire, appraise, apply, assess.
"No evidence" often means not studied yet, and evidence never overrides safety.

next.title: Why Treatments Seem to Work When They May Not

title: Why Treatments Seem to Work When They May Not

hook.en: A patient comes in with terrible pain. You treat them. Two weeks later they are better and thank you. Did your treatment work? Maybe. But four other things could also explain the recovery, and a good therapist learns to think of all five.
hook.ur: Mareez shadeed dard ke saath aata hai. Aap ilaaj karte hain. Do haftay baad woh behtar hai aur shukriya kehta hai. Kya aap ke ilaaj ne kaam kiya? Shayad. Lekin recovery ki char aur wajuhaat bhi ho sakti hain, aur achha therapist paanchon ke baare mein sochna seekhta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll name five reasons a treatment can look effective without being so (natural history, regression to the mean, placebo and context, co-interventions, confounding), explain why control groups exist, and talk about this honestly with patients.
goal.ur: End tak aap paanch wajuhaat batayenge jin ki wajah se ilaaj kaam karta lagta hai bina asar ke (natural history, regression to the mean, placebo aur context, co-interventions, confounding), samjhayenge ke control groups kyun hote hain, aur mareezon se is par imaandari se baat karenge.

summaryEn: Natural history, regression to the mean, context, co-interventions and confounding can all make a treatment look effective.
Only a fair comparison group separates what the treatment did from what would have happened anyway.
Context effects are real, can be used ethically, and never replace safe assessment or referral.

title: From Clinical Question to PICO in Five Minutes

hook.en: "Does exercise help back pain?" is not a question you can search for. "In adults with chronic low back pain, does supervised exercise reduce pain more than advice alone at three months?" is. Learn how to turn a worry into a question that finds an answer.
hook.ur: "Kya exercise peeth dard mein madad karti hai?" aisa sawal nahi jo dhoondha ja sake. title: Maitland Joint Mobilization

hook.en: Gentle, rhythmic rocking of a joint, graded I to IV by how far into the range you go, chosen by how irritable the patient's pain is.
hook.ur: Maitland Joint Mobilization mein therapist joint ko patient ki taraf se relax halat mein chhoti, narm aur rhythm ke sath aagay-peechay harkat deta hai.

summaryEn: In one line: Test the movement, choose the glide and grade, test the movement again.
Use it for: A painful, stiff joint where one movement clearly reproduces the patient's pain (positive comparable sign).

next.title: Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization

title: Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization

hook.en: Mobilization that uses joint shape (the convex-concave rule) to pick the glide direction, and traction grades to loosen, take up slack, or stretch.
hook.ur: Kaltenborn–Evjenth approach mein joint par sustained traction ya glide diya jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Kaltenborn–Evjenth Mobilization kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Know the joint shape, choose the glide direction, escalate the stage only if the joint is calm.
Use it for: A joint that moves less than the other side with a firm, capsular-type end-feel.
Stop or avoid when: Unstable joints, acute fractures, active infection or inflammation, and suspected tumour.

next.title: Manual Traction & Joint Distraction

title: Manual Traction & Joint Distraction

hook.en: A gentle pull that separates joint surfaces to reduce compression and test or calm symptoms.
hook.ur: Manual traction ya joint distraction mein joint ko controlled direction mein ahista kheench kar compression-sensitive symptoms ka response dekha jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Manual Traction & Joint Distraction is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Manual Traction & Joint Distraction kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Less pressure, then test: if traction eases the symptom, the joint is involved.
Use it for: Joint pain that eases when compression is removed.
Stop or avoid when: Instability, fracture, infection, or rheumatoid involvement of the upper neck.

next.title: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM)

title: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM)

hook.en: A sustained joint glide applied by the therapist while the patient performs the movement that normally hurts, aiming for an instant pain-free result.
hook.ur: Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM) mein therapist ek sustained accessory glide deta hai aur patient usi waqt apni active movement karta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM) is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Mulligan Mobilization With Movement (MWM) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Glide, move, ask: if it is not pain-free and instant, it is not the right glide.
Use it for: A clearly painful or restricted movement that is easy to repeat, for example painful gripping at the elbow or restricted ankle dorsiflexion.
Stop or avoid when: No immediate pain-free improvement after a few careful tries.

next.title: Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs

title: Mulligan NAGs, SNAGs & Self-SNAGs

hook.en: Neck and spine glides applied along the facet joint while the patient moves actively (SNAG) or in gentle oscillation (NAG).
hook.ur: NAGs, SNAGs aur Self-SNAGs spinal mobilization ke tareeqay hain jin mein joint ki glide ko passive ya active movement ke sath combine kiya jata hai.

summaryEn: In one line: Glide along the facet, move the neck, and keep it pain-free.

title: PAIVM & PPIVM Spinal Assessment / Mobilization

hook.en: Hands-on spinal examination: PPIVMs test movement between vertebrae through natural bends; PAIVMs test small glides between them.
hook.ur: PAIVM aur PPIVM spinal assessment ke tareeqay hain: PAIVM mein accessory pressure aur PPIVM mein spine ki physiological movement assess ki jati hai.

next.title: HVLA Thrust Manipulation

title: HVLA Thrust Manipulation

hook.en: A fast, small, controlled thrust at the end of a joint's range, used only after careful screening and supervised training.
hook.ur: HVLA manipulation ek rapid aur chhoti-range thrust hai jo sirf appropriate examination, informed consent aur safety screening ke baad trained clinician perform karta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what HVLA Thrust Manipulation is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke HVLA Thrust Manipulation kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

next.title: Neurodynamic Mobilization

title: Neurodynamic Mobilization

hook.en: Gentle movements that slide or lightly tension a nerve so it moves freely and tolerates movement better.
hook.ur: Neurodynamic mobilization mein nervous system aur us ke aas-paas ke tissues ki movement tolerance par kaam kiya jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Neurodynamic Mobilization is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Neurodynamic Mobilization kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Slide first, tension later, and never provoke sharp or lingering symptoms.
Use it for: Arm or leg symptoms (tingling, aching, pulling) reproduced by neural tension positions with a clear pattern.

next.title: PNF Manual Techniques

title: PNF Manual Techniques

hook.en: Using the patient's own gentle muscle contractions, with your hand resistance, to improve range, strength and control.
hook.ur: PNF manual techniques mein therapist ki resistance, stretch aur diagonal movement patterns use hotay hain taake coordinated movement aur functional motor control ko facilitate kiya ja sake.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what PNF Manual Techniques is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke PNF Manual Techniques kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Gentle contraction, full relaxation, then move into the new range.

next.title: Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction

title: Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction

hook.ur: Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction mein symptomatic tendon, ligament ya muscle ke tissue par us ke fibres ki direction ke aar-paar localized pressure aur movement di jati hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Cyriax Deep Transverse Friction kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Find the exact spot, rub across the fibres, then load the tendon.

next.title: Muscle Energy Technique (MET)

title: Muscle Energy Technique (MET)

hook.en: A gentle muscle contraction by the patient against your precise resistance, followed by a stretch or movement into the new range.
hook.ur: Muscle Energy Technique (MET) mein patient apni muscle se controlled contraction karta hai aur therapist munasib resistance deta hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Muscle Energy Technique (MET) is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Muscle Energy Technique (MET) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Light push, full relax, then move to the new barrier.

next.title: Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release

title: Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release

hook.en: Finding a tender point, then holding the body in the position of most comfort for about 90 seconds to settle it.
hook.ur: Strain Counterstrain ya positional release ek indirect approach hai: sensitive area ko aisi position mein le jaya jata hai jahan patient ko zyada comfort ho, phir dheere se neutral position mein wapas laya jata hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Strain Counterstrain / Positional Release kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Find the sore point, move toward ease, hold, return slowly.

next.title: Facilitated Positional Release (FPR)

title: Facilitated Positional Release (FPR)

hook.en: A short, gentle method: find the neutral position of a tight area, add a small compression, then move toward comfort for a few seconds.
hook.ur: Facilitated Positional Release (FPR) ek indirect positional technique hai bodye region ko relative comfort mein rakh kar gentle facilitating force di jati hai.

goal.en: By the end, you'll know what Facilitated Positional Release (FPR) is, when it's safe and useful, how to apply it step by step — and how to prove it worked. (3 checks along the way.)
goal.ur: End tak aap jaan jayenge ke Facilitated Positional Release (FPR) kya hai, kab safe aur faida-mand hai, qadam ba qadam kaise apply hoti hai — aur kaise prove karein ke kaam kiya. (Raste mein 3 checks.)

summaryEn: In one line: Neutral, light compression, ease, short hold, retest.
Use it for: Tight, tender muscle areas that are sensitive to firm treatment.
Stop or avoid when: Fracture, instability or unexplained severe pain.

next.title: Myofascial Release (Direct & Indirect)

title: Myofascial Release (Direct & Indirect)
